option_relations.rationale: The option describes a specific genetic form of cerebral small vessel disease, which is not directly related to Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA) as an equivalent, subtype, or supertype. While both involve small vessels, HTRA1-related CSVD is distinct from CAA.
Hypertensive Small Vessel Disease is a distinct etiology of cerebral small vessel disease, separate from Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy. They are not equivalent, subtype, or supertype of each other.

Hereditary Cerebral Small Vessel Disease (HTRA1-related) is a specific genetic form of small vessel disease, which is not directly related to Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA) as an equivalent, subtype, or supertype. While both involve small vessels, HTRA1-related CSVD is distinct from CAA.

Heterozygous HTRA1-related cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) is a specific genetic form of small vessel disease, which is not directly related to Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy (CAA) as an equivalent, subtype, or supertype. While both involve small vessels, HTRA1-related CSVD is distinct from CAA.
